title: Continuous batcher: soft-reserve policy + opportunistic KV defrag playbook for mixed-length streams
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Mixed prompt/response workloads (chat + code completions) create hotspots in KV residency and GPU slab fragmentation. Long-response turns pin large KV slices; short-turn bursts suffer slot starvation and increased evictions, increasing token cost and p95 latency. Goal: tune the continuous batching scheduler to reduce eviction churn and GPU memory fragmentation while preserving p50/p95 latency SLOs and lowering unit token cost for mixed-length traffic.

Proposal summary: implement a soft-reserve policy in the continuous batcher + opportunistic KV defragmentation (compaction) playbook. The soft-reserve policy gives a small, dynamic KV reservation for streams predicted to require long responses while remaining probabilistic at high load to avoid wasted residency. The opportunistic defrag process runs low-priority background passes when GPU utilization < 40% for > 250ms, coalescing small free regions and trimming KV slabs for short-lived streams. Combine with admission tweaks (probabilistic acceptance for long-turn requests when memory pressure is high) and an adaptive shrink threshold that uses recent eviction churn and KV hit-rate as signals.

Success metrics:
- Reduce KV eviction churn by >= 20% for mixed-length synthetic workload.
- Maintain p95 generation latency within +10ms of baseline on canary traffic.
- Reduce per-token GPU memory overhead (measured as average resident KB/token) by >= 6% across test workloads.
- No customer-facing errors or increased OOM incidents during canary rollout.

Why different from prior efforts: earlier tickets focused on batching window heuristics, slot coalescing, and strict reservation. This work focuses on a pragmatic middle ground: 'soft' reservations + opportunistic cleanup to address fragmentation rather than larger structural allocator rewrites. The goal is low-risk iterative rollout with measurable cost/latency improvements.
acceptance_criteria: Feature gated behind batcher.soft_reserve and runtime.opportunistic_kv_defrag flags
Canary run at 5% traffic for 72h with automated rollback on >=2 SLA breaches
End-to-end benchmarks showing KV eviction churn reduction >=20% and token overhead reduction >=6%
Operational dashboards: KV-residency heatmap, eviction-rate, p50/p95 latency, GPU util and free-region histogram added to Console runtime-1.24 dashboard
Playbook documented in Confluence and linked in ticket
work_plan: Design: define soft-reserve algorithm (per-stream predicted_length -> reserved_kb formula) and probabilistic admission curve (sigmoid based on free_bytes/gpu_slab) - owner: Marco
Prototype: implement in the batcher simulator and run offline mixed-length traces (internal trace corpus + production sampled traces) - owner: Marco
Microbenchmark: quantify eviction churn and p95 on synthetic mixes (20% long/80% short; 50%/50%; and heavy bursts). Record baseline and variant numbers - owner: SRE
Implement runtime feature flag and lightweight metrics (kv_reserved, kv_evictions, kv_compactions, free_region_count) - owner: infra
Canary: 5% customer traffic for 72h with automated rollback on errors/SLO breaches - owner: ops
Rollout: 25% -> 50% -> 100% with monitoring and staged config tuning - owner: product/ops
Postmortem: collect memory fragmentation traces and update compaction heuristics if needed - owner: Marco

notes_and_tradeoffs: Trade-off: soft-reserve reduces eviction churn for long-streams at the cost of some reserved memory which can slightly increase average resident memory. We reduce risk by making reservations probabilistic under high pressure.
Trade-off: opportunistic defrag introduces small CPU overhead and low-priority GPU passes; we gate it on low-util conditions to avoid latency impact.

Alternative considered: rewrite allocator to use buddy/segregated-slab hybrid. Rejected due to high rollout risk and long implementation time; soft-reserve + defrag provides most benefits with lower risk.
Future: integrate a learned predictor for response length to better size soft reservations and reduce false positives. This is scoped as a follow-up (post-rollout)
